parts.title: What they cover
lines: `prepare-commands` (exact): The list of commands is what the step's rule gives again over the inputs its provenance record names: a result that does not follow from its recorded inputs is found.
`verify-answer` (exact): The answer counts only where it matches the pattern `^42$`.

parts.title: What they do not cover
lines: `prepare-commands` (exact): The list of commands computed from inputs that were themselves wrong passes, and so does a rule that computes the wrong thing the same way every time.
`compute` (tolerant): the step declares no check, so no wrong result of it is found by one.
`verify-answer` (exact): A wrong value of the answer that matches the pattern `^42$` passes.
`overreach` (tolerant): the step declares no check, so no wrong result of it is found by one.

parts.title: The residual risk
lines: `prepare-commands` (exact): a wrong result slips through only where every check misses it at once — wrong inputs, or a rule that computes the wrong thing.
`compute` (tolerant): every wrong result slips through; no check applies to it.
`verify-answer` (exact): a wrong result slips through only where every check misses it at once — a wrong value that matches the pattern `^42$`.
`overreach` (tolerant): every wrong result slips through; no check applies to it.

findings.text:
Product finding: no worker offers code.review

An instance of Taktus met something the product lacks. A step needed a worker that offers `code.review`. No configured worker offers it. The step failed for it, and its run waited until the step could start again.

What would resolve it: the product offers `code.review` among its workers, through an adapter or an operation of one it has, or says why it does not.

Where it was met: run `run_example`, step `draft`, cause `no_worker`, as the blocked-time accounts of the instance record it (UC-6.12).
